items.title: Innovation vs. Novelty: The Distinction Every Scrum Master Must Master
items.excerpt: In 1947, as nations across the globe were redrawing their futures, a company called Convair unveiled something extraordinary: the Convair Model 118 — a flying car. Only two were ever built. Was it innovation? Not quite. It was a clever mashup, a car bolted to an aircraft, an ingenious combination, but not a transformation. At best, it was a novelty. Perhaps it was ahead of its time. Perhaps a world still recovering from war simply had no appetite for it. But the deeper reason it never took off — literally or figuratively — is this: it didn't meaningfully change how people traveled. It was new.
